by God extraordinarily, to save his rebellious subjects out of the hands of the enemy. It
cannot be drawn into argument against the right the high priest had to the sober reign
power in all matters, both of policy and religion. And neither the Judges nor Samuel himself
had an ordinary, but extraordinary calling to the government, and were obeyed by the
Israelites not out of duty, but out of reverence to their favor with God, appearing in their
wisdom, courage, or felicity. Hitherto therefore the right of regulating both the policy and
